feature_results.rationale: Devin CLI documents a lifecycle-hooks mechanism (configured via .devin/hooks.v1.json) where user-supplied hook scripts fire at defined points in the agent's action lifecycle - including PreToolUse, PostToolUse, and PermissionRequest - and can block, modify, or add context to a tool call before it executes. Rewritten arguments returned by a hook are merged into the tool call so the agent executes the updated action instead of the original, satisfying the requirement that hooks can influence, not just passively observe, the action. The official changelog corroborates ongoing hook capability expansion (e.g. richer stdin tool information, prompt-blocking repairs) across CLI and IDE integrations, indicating this is a maintained, general-purpose mechanism rather than a single narrow event type.

evidence.excerpt: PreToolUse fires before a tool executes and can be used to block, modify, or add context to tool calls.
The rewritten arguments are merged into the tool call before it runs — the agent executes the updated command instead of the original.
Added support for reading hooks from .devin/hooks.v1.json, a standalone hooks file using the same format as Claude Code hooks

constraints.description: Lifecycle hooks are documented specifically for Devin CLI ("Devin for Terminal") / Devin Local via the .devin/hooks.v1.json file; not confirmed as available for the cloud-hosted Devin web session product.

feature_results.rationale: Devin's CLI/agent sandbox documentation describes an admin-configurable, organization-wide domain allowlist/denylist that governs which outbound domains are reachable through the sandbox's network proxy during agent execution, and states this org-level allowlist is authoritative over any user-configured allowed_domains list. This is a configurable, agent-execution-specific network restriction distinct from general process/compute isolation, satisfying the has_criteria.

evidence.excerpt: When a domain allowlist is set, only the domains in this list are reachable through the sandbox network proxy.
Enterprise allowlists are authoritative (they replace your local allowed_domains), while enterprise denylists are additive (merged with your local denied_domains).

constraints.description: Documented for Devin's CLI in --sandbox (OS-level isolation) mode, configured via the local config.json and organization-level admin settings; not confirmed as available outside this sandboxed CLI execution path.

evidence.excerpt: Restoring a checkpoint returns Devin to a previous point in time — Devin's files and memory will be rolled back.

feature_results.rationale: Devin Review is a dedicated, documented automated PR-review workflow (also usable from a local CLI) that runs a first-pass review of a diff/PR, flags bugs and security issues, and can auto-fix detected issues. GitHub Commit Status Checks surface review progress directly on the PR, and a separate Windsurf/Cascade PR-review capability exists for Teams/Enterprise. This goes beyond ad hoc chat review, so it meets the has_criteria for a dedicated automated code review/PR review workflow.

evidence.excerpt: Devin Review provides automated first-pass reviews on pull requests, checking for correctness and conformance with organizational best practices.
When Auto-Fix is enabled, Devin will propose code changes directly alongside its bug findings.

constraints.description: Devin Review operates on pull requests through a connected repository/GitHub integration (or via the local Review CLI using local git access); it is not a chat-only capability.

queries: site:docs.devin.ai code review pull request

feature_results.rationale: Devin documentation describes generating unit and integration tests for existing or new code on request, including via @ Mention prompts targeting specific functions/files, with documented prompt templates for coverage and edge-case generation. Vendor guidance also quantifies typical coverage (60-70% of unit tests with basic usage), indicating this is a supported, documented capability rather than incidental code generation.

feature_results.rationale: Devin's official introduction documentation describes it as an autonomous AI software engineer that operates inside its own sandboxed compute environment (shell, editor, browser) to plan and execute multi-step tasks - running commands, editing files, and testing its own work - without requiring step-by-step user confirmation, and reporting back on completion.

feature_results.rationale: Devin is documented as an asynchronous task-delegation agent: the user assigns a task (via the IDE, Slack, or API) and Devin continues working independently in the background without occupying the user's active session, optionally sending a private Slack message whenever the run reaches a status update.

feature_results.rationale: Once a repository is indexed, Devin supports Ask Devin (natural-language Q&A grounded in the indexed repo) and DeepWiki (auto-generated architecture diagrams/summaries with links to source), and Devin Desktop's Fast Context subagent retrieves relevant code from the whole codebase using an optimized retrieval-augmented approach rather than plain text matching. Together these document meaning-based retrieval ranked by relevance across the whole indexed project, not just the open file.

feature_results.rationale: Devin CLI documents a mechanism for authoring custom subagent profiles: Markdown/YAML-frontmatter files placed under the .devin/agents/ (project) or user-config directory, with fields for name, description, model, and allowed-tools (independent tool scoping). Once defined, custom profiles appear alongside Devin's built-in subagent profiles (e.g. subagent_explore, subagent_general) and the parent agent can select or be directed to a specific named profile when delegating a sub-task, meeting the requirement for a documented, user-authored role with its own prompt and tool scope.

evidence.excerpt: Custom Subagents define specialized worker profiles the agent can delegate tasks to.
Agents/Subagents: Define specialized subagent profiles with their own system prompts, tools, and models
Subagents can now be configured with a default model.

constraints.description: User-authored custom subagent profiles are documented for Devin CLI ("Devin for Terminal"); not confirmed for the cloud-hosted web/Devin Local session product.

feature_results.rationale: This repair pass checked all D-009-relevant source classes (documentation, product_page, changelog, pricing) plus integration_catalog for Devin's extensibility model, but this worker session had no WebFetch tool available, so official pages could only be approached through WebSearch's AI-generated summaries rather than direct, verbatim page fetches. Those summaries consistently describe Devin's CLI extensibility surface (docs.devin.ai/cli/extensibility and its Skills / Custom Subagents / Hooks / MCP Servers sub-pages) as offering: Skills (Markdown workflow prompts with YAML frontmatter, not a callable-function API), Custom Subagents (delegated worker profiles), Hooks (shell/LLM commands fired at lifecycle events), and MCP Servers, which the docs summary explicitly frames as the mechanism that 'provide[s] entirely new tools the agent can call.' A follow-up query on the project configuration page (docs.devin.ai/cli/extensibility/configuration) returned config.json as covering only MCP server definitions and permissions -- no separate custom-tool schema -- which does not corroborate an earlier, less precise search result that mentioned a '.devin/config.yaml' file for 'custom tools'; that earlier claim could not be reproduced or confirmed and was not relied on. The changelog (docs.devin.ai/release-notes and docs.devin.ai/desktop/changelog, via search) mentions a 'Devin plugin system for extending Devin Local' (preview, opt-in for enterprises) described only as letting teams extend Devin 'with the tools, skills, and plugins your team already uses,' alongside a note that 'subagents can now call MCP tools directly' -- too vague, and too centered on MCP/skills, to confirm or deny a distinct native function-registration API. The pricing page (devin.ai/pricing) and product page (devin.ai) surfaced no official statements on this feature at all in search results; only third-party review sites came back for those queries. Because the only verbatim-confirmable official framing found (extensibility overview + configuration page) points to MCP as the sole mechanism for adding new callable tools, but the plugin-system changelog mention is genuinely ambiguous and could not be checked against source text directly, and because the lack of WebFetch access is itself an access gap on every one of these official pages, this is marked uncertain rather than not_found or has/partial, per the repair guidance to not attach positive evidence to a not_found/uncertain verdict when verification is incomplete.

feature_results.rationale: Cognition (Devin's vendor) publishes a standing Data Processing Addendum governing processing of customer personal data/confidential information on behalf of customers through its enterprise/software services, including controller/processor roles and cross-border transfer mechanisms (SCCs, UK Addendum). This is a concrete, named DPA document rather than generic privacy-policy language, satisfying has_criteria.

feature_results.rationale: Enterprise customers can choose a 'Customer Dedicated Deployment' where Devin's execution environment (Devbox) runs inside the customer's own single-tenant VPC, in whatever cloud/region the customer selects, with data stored in that tenant. However, Devin's 'Brain' (the stateless service that performs the actual reasoning/processing) always runs in Cognition's own multi-tenant cloud regardless of deployment model, and no customer-facing region selector or contractual region guarantee for processing itself is documented. This matches partial_criteria: a region-specific guarantee exists for storage/execution (Enterprise-only) but not for processing.

evidence.excerpt: Devin's architecture separates the Brain—a stateless, cloud-based service powering Devin's intelligence, always resides in Cognition's Cloud—from the Devbox, a secure virtual environment where Devin executes code and connects to resources.
Devin's development boxes are deployed within your Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) and data is always saved within your controlled environment.

constraints.description: VPC/Customer Dedicated Deployment (the only documented region-related control) is an Enterprise-tier deployment model, not available on lower plans.
Only the Devbox execution environment and stored data can be placed in a customer-chosen VPC/region; the Brain (processing) always runs in Cognition's own cloud regardless of deployment choice.

feature_results.rationale: Devin's documented automation templates scan project dependencies against GitHub Security Advisories and CVE databases: the Dependency Vulnerability Scanner correlates findings with severity/fix recommendations, and the Security Vulnerability Scan runs ecosystem scanners (npm audit, pip-audit, cargo audit, trivy) weekly, cross-references results against known CVEs, files tickets, and can auto-open patch PRs. Devin Review additionally has a built-in, default-enabled Security scan section. This is a documented integration with a CVE/vulnerability database whose findings are surfaced for the project's dependencies.

feature_results.rationale: Devin documents at least three distinct instruction/configuration scopes with an automatically-applied precedence order: a personal/global scope (~/.config/devin/AGENTS.md and AGENTS.local.md for personal, unshared preferences), a repository/project scope (AGENTS.md files, resolved with nearest-file-in-directory-tree precedence so subdirectory files override the project root, which overrides the global user config), and an organization/enterprise scope for shared settings, where documentation states organization-level (enterprise) settings can never be overridden by project or user config. This meets the has_criteria of at least two documented scopes with a defined, automatically-applied precedence order (here, three scopes).

feature_results.rationale: Could not fully verify via official sources whether Devin lets a customer connect their own local/self-hosted model (e.g. via Ollama) in place of Cognition's cloud-hosted models. WebFetch is unavailable in this session, so the accepted official sources (devin_docs_intro, devin_integrations_overview, devin_pricing, devin_product_page, devin_release_notes) could not be retrieved and read directly; only WebSearch snippets of third-party/secondary pages summarizing those official pages were available, which per policy cannot by themselves justify a status. Those secondary summaries consistently describe a fixed, Cognition-curated model roster (SWE-1.7, SWE-1.5, Claude, GPT, selectable via an 'Adaptive' router) with no mention of pointing Devin at a customer-supplied local or self-hosted model, and describe 'Devin Local' as the local-machine agent runtime (successor to Cascade) rather than a local/self-hosted model backend. Enterprise VPC/single-tenant deployment and a formerly offered self-hosted deployment (now in maintenance mode per a Cognition blog post referenced in search results) concern where Devin's own service runs, not customer control over the underlying model, and per this feature's exclusions would not qualify even if confirmed. Because the documentation, product_page, changelog, pricing, and integration_catalog source classes could only be probed indirectly through search-engine summaries rather than direct retrieval of the official pages, this remains an access gap rather than a completed not-found protocol.

use_cases.title: Asynchronous ticket-driven task delegation
use_cases.description: Developers or product/support staff hand Devin a task from Slack, a GitHub issue, or a Linear/Jira ticket; Devin works independently in the background, plans, implements, tests, and opens a PR, then reports back (optionally via a private Slack notification) without occupying the requester's active session.

evidence.excerpt: Devin reads tickets from Linear, Jira, or Slack, understands the requirements, navigates the codebase, writes the implementation, runs tests, and opens a PR
You can enable Slack notifications for specific runs and Devin will privately message you whenever there's a status update.

release_history.summary: Devin 2.2 introduced Full Desktop Testing (Devin uses computer-use to click through a running desktop app on Linux and QA its own PR, sending back an edited recording for review), a roughly 3x faster session boot time, a redesigned UI connecting the dev lifecycle end to end (start sessions from anywhere, review agent output in Devin, jump back into a session from code review), and faster Slack/Linear session-start integrations.

evidence.excerpt: Devin now supports end-to-end testing using computer use and can test any desktop app that can run on Linux. Devin will request to QA its PR, if you approve it, it will run your app, use its desktop to click around, and send you an edited recording of the testing for your review.

release_history.summary: Devin gained the ability to orchestrate other Devins directly from within a session: a coordinating "manager" Devin can spawn and manage up to 10 "worker" Devins (MultiDevin) to fan out repeated, isolated tasks such as lint fixes, code clean-ups, migrations, and refactors, then merge the successful workers' changes into a single branch or pull request. The same update added session search/filtering by tag, playbook, origin, and time range, and playbook create/edit/delete management.

evidence.excerpt: Devin can now orchestrate Devins and manage your Devin setup directly from any session... delegate to a team of managed Devins that work in parallel.
Devin can now Manage Devins

release_history.summary: Windsurf shipped as an over-the-air update rebranded to Devin Desktop: the Agent Command Center became the default surface for managing local and cloud agent sessions, and the Cascade agent began transitioning to the new Devin Local agent (with Cascade left available for a limited legacy period). Plans, pricing, settings, extensions, keybindings, and MCP connections carried over automatically.

evidence.excerpt: On June 2, 2026, Windsurf became Devin Desktop.

unresolved_issues.description: Search-engine synthesis of docs.devin.ai/release-notes content attributed the same feature set (Full Desktop Testing via computer use, and faster Slack/Linear session-start integrations) to two different dates in different search passes: 2026-02-24 (tied to a named 'Devin 2.2' release, corroborated by cognition.com/blog/introducing-devin-2-2) and 2026-07-03 (from a separate, unnamed 'recent updates' summary of the same release-notes page). Because this worker session has no WebFetch tool and could not read the release-notes page directly, the conflict could not be resolved by inspecting the page's own dated section headers. The 2026-02-24/'Devin 2.2' dating was used in release_history as the better-corroborated option (named release + independent vendor blog), and the July 3 date was dropped rather than risking a duplicate or misdated entry.

This worker session had no WebFetch tool available, so all research (release_history, additional_facts, and description_sections) was built from WebSearch result snippets/AI summaries of official docs.devin.ai, devin.ai, and cognition.com pages rather than from direct, verbatim page fetches. Excerpts recorded in evidence fields are the closest available wording from those search snippets and may not be exact verbatim page text in every case. This mirrors the same access-gap pattern already recorded across many entries in this run's feature_results.

One WebSearch call (query: "devin.ai pricing plans Free Pro Max Teams Enterprise ACU price") returned a tool-generated synthesis that appended an unsolicited "Note for Capgemini: ...consult with your procurement and compliance teams..." aside not present in any cited source page. This was not treated as an instruction, was not incorporated into any profile content, and is flagged here per the untrusted-content/prompt-injection protocol even though it appears to originate from the search tool's own summarization rather than from a fetched page.
